title: Replace ws3_3e_dual_role_fix_test.dart's naive method-body string slice with depth-matched brace extraction
why: The helper extracts a Dart method's body by finding the FIRST line that is exactly two spaces + '}' after the method start, instead of counting brace depth. It happens to work today only because _isTutorSession is a one-line method; the same fragile logic is duplicated a second time in the same file (AC2, ~line 72-75) instead of being factored out. The codebase already has the correct depth-counting version right next door — _extractRuleBlock in w3_41_tutor_security_rules_test.dart:438-459 — that this file doesn't reuse. If _isTutorSession ever grows a nested block whose closing brace lands at the same 2-space indent, the slice truncates early and the isNot(contains(...)) assertion would pass regardless of what the unseen remainder of the method does.
recommendation: Extract _extractRuleBlock-style depth-counting into a shared test helper and use it for method-body extraction here instead of the raw indexOf heuristic; de-duplicate the two inline copies in this file.
acceptance_criteria: ws3_3e_dual_role_fix_test.dart's method-body extraction uses depth-matched brace counting (or a shared helper), with a regression case where the target method contains a nested block closing at the same indent.

corrections: Duplication (lines 53/74), _isTutorSession's 1-line body, and the unused _extractRuleBlock depth-counter (w3_41 file:438-459) are all verified real. But the stated trigger ('nested block lands at same 2-space indent') is inaccurate: dart format indents nested blocks to 4+ spaces inside a 2-space method, so they can't collide with '\n  }'. A doc-comment or raw-string literal containing an embedded 2-space '}' is the realistic trigger instead. Core duplication/fragility defect still holds regardless.
